item.title: Turing bifurcation, criticality, and multistability in a nonlocal advection-reaction-diffusion equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.21398v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper considers a nonlocal advection--reaction--diffusion equation with logistic growth. We investigate how the interaction kernel affects the criticality of Turing bifurcations and the associated multistability. We first prove that nonhomogeneous stationary solutions bifurcate from the positive homogeneous stationary solution. Center manifold reduction yields an amplitude equation near the bifurcation point. This equation provides criteria for supercritical and subcritical bifurcations in terms of the Fourier transform of the interaction kernel. We also derive a sufficient condition for subcriticality. This condition can be satisfied by sufficiently localized attractive interactions. Based on these analytical results, we investigate multistability through numerical bifurcation analysis. The numerical results show that the stable homogeneous stationary solution can coexist with stable nonhomogeneous stationary solutions or stable time-periodic solutions.
item.dc:creator: Yui Nagayama, Masaharu Nagayama, Hiroshi Ishii

item.title: Vortex clusters and vortex-filled bubbles in a modified Abelian-Higgs model
item.description: arXiv:2610.21930v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate a single-component Abelian-Higgs model with an eighth-order scalar potential whose vacuum manifold consists of two disconnected circles. The model supports two species of vortices and domain walls interpolating between the two vacuum components. We find type-1.5-like behavior characterized by nonmonotonic intervortex interactions and bound states of spatially separated vortices. Inner-vacuum vortices form clusters through short-range repulsion and long-range attraction, whereas outer-vacuum vortices form vortex-filled bubbles in which a closed domain wall confines multiple inner-vacuum-vortex cores. We construct the domain wall analytically, derive the asymptotic vortex-wall interactions, and analyze the fluctuation spectra of coincident multivortices to identify their splitting instabilities.
item.dc:creator: D. Migu\'elez-Caballero, S. Navarro-Obreg\'on, Muneto Nitta, Keisuke Ohashi

item.title: Cone Invariance and Homoclinic Standing Waves for Cooperative Finite-Range DNLS Equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.22166v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a constrained-power variational framework for positive homoclinic standing waves in one-dimensional discrete nonlinear Schr\"odinger equations with cooperative finite-range interactions. Starting from periodic lattices, we construct constrained energy maximizers and use the associated projected gradient flow to establish positive invariance of the cone of nonnegative, even, and unimodal profiles. A central result is that the monotone ordering of the interaction coefficients, \(a_1\ge a_2\ge\cdots\ge a_M\ge0\), with \(a_1>0\), provides the structural condition ensuring preservation of this cone under finite-range coupling. Under a strict maximum condition above the linear spectral edge, we obtain a uniform frequency gap and period-independent exponential localization. These estimates provide the compactness required for the infinite-period limit and yield positive, even, unimodal, and exponentially localized homoclinic standing waves as strong \(\ell^2(\mathbb Z)\)-limits of periodic constrained maximizers. Numerical computations for several interaction ranges and cooperative kernels illustrate the effects of extended coupling on dispersion and localization and support the periodic-to-homoclinic convergence predicted by the analysis.
item.dc:creator: Vassilios M. Rothos

item.title: Minimum nonlinearity for pattern-forming Turing instability in a mathematical autocatalytic model
item.description: arXiv:2412.13783v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Pattern formation is ubiquitous in nature and the mechanism widely-accepted to underlay them is based on the Turing instability, predicted by Alan Turing decades ago. This is a non-trivial mechanism that involves nonlinear interaction terms between the different species involved and transport mechanisms. We present here a mathematical analysis aiming to explore the mathematical constraints that a reaction-diffusion dynamical model should comply in order to exhibit a Turing instability. The main conclusion limits the existence of this instability to nonlinearity degrees larger or equal to three.
item.dc:creator: Javier L\'opez-Pedrares, Marcos Su\'arez-V\'azquez, Juan P\'erez-Mercader, Alberto P. Mu\~nuzuri

item.title: Collision Dynamics of False-Vacuum Oscillons
item.description: arXiv:2605.12633v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the collision dynamics of localized oscillons in two classes of $(1+1)$-dimensional scalar field theories with metastable false vacua, a normal class with a positive quartic self-interaction term and an inverted class with a negative quartic term. We construct small-amplitude oscillon solutions around the false vacuum using the Fodor {\emph{et al.}} expansion, and show that the force between oscillons decays exponentially at large separation, with a strength modulated by their relative phase. Numerical simulations of two-oscillon collisions exhibit reflection, crossing, and formation of excited oscillons. Resonance windows occur, similar to those found in kink-antikink collisions. In the normal theory, if the oscillons have sufficient energy, the field can pass over a sphaleron barrier and evolve into a kink-antikink pair, initiating a phase transition to the true vacuum. We also simulate the collision of oscillons evolved from a slightly perturbed sphaleron.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: J. G. F. Campos, N. S. Manton and A. Mohammadi, Collision Dynamics of False-Vacuum Oscillons, JHEP 08 (2026) 109
item.dc:creator: J. G. F. Campos, N. S. Manton, Azadeh Mohammadi

item.title: Real-time identification of the onset of financial rogue waves
item.description: arXiv:2606.31475v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Extreme events in financial systems, often captured by indicators such as volatility, remain difficult to identify close to their onset. Volatility shares many statistical properties with other natural, complex systems which experience extreme events, which we explore in this manuscript. We extend the analogy between rogue waves in optical and hydrodynamical systems to financial volatility by identifying rogue-wave-like peaks with similar statistical properties. We use a Schr\"odinger equation where the potential follows the shape of a Kerr nonlinearity to examine the properties of financial volatility indices within a moving time window. We see evidence of Anderson localisation as a rogue peak approaches in the VIX, and show that the numerical gradient of the system's minimum eigenvalue reliably spikes at the onset of an extreme event. We adapt our methodology to simulate the real-time arrival of data, and show that all but one of the VIX's major peaks can be detected given a reasonable amount of history. We then perform two out-of-sample tests, one for the VXO index, and one for the VSTOXX index, and successfully replicate our initial results, identifying all but one major peak (87.5% or 7/8) in both cases. This method of analysis shows considerable promise as a tool for identifying potential financial crises, aiding in their mitigation.
item.dc:creator: Rosie Hayward, Orla Lennon, Fabio Biancalana
